clue.text: Chicken pieces for battering

definitions.meaning: the lower leg joints of a fowl, served as finger food
the sticks a percussionist uses to beat a drum

explanation.surface: A recipe note: these bits of chicken are the ones to coat in batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battering' seems to mean coating in batter for frying; it really means beating, as one beats a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the cooked legs of a bird and the beaters a percussionist holds share this name.

clue.text: Sapper's attitude to the rest

parts.note: a sapper is a soldier of the Royal Engineers, RE

explanation.surface: A military engineer's view of everybody else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the rest' looks like 'the others'; it means relaxation.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of relaxation or calm is a time of ease and inactivity.

clue.text: Something very short and snappy in espionage

definitions.text: Something very short and snappy in espionage

parts.words: Something very short and snappy in espionage
parts.note: short means tiny and snappy means photographed: a spy's minute photograph

explanation.surface: A brief, punchy item in the world of spies.
explanation.definitionFit: Spies shrink documents photographically to a speck the size of a full stop.

clue.text: Performed acrobatics and won somehow, though threatening to fall

indicators.note: somehow means the letters of the word won are juggled into another order

explanation.surface: A gymnast won a contest despite looking ready to collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' turns WON into OWN, added after TUMBLED.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilapidated building looks ready to collapse into ruin.

clue.text: Accountant takes round trip in fairness

annotationWithheld.why: Accountant takes round trip in fairness (7): CA (accountant) leaves NDOUR, and no reading of 'takes round trip' gives those letters; the clue as held looks misprinted
annotationWithheld.clue: Accountant takes round trip in fairness

clue.text: Society takes ages to get antitoxins

parts.note: a long period of time, an epoch

explanation.surface: A society spends years producing antitoxins.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood fluids containing antibodies are given as antidotes to poisons.

clue.text: Self-banking aircraft?

parts.note: auto means self, and the giro is a bank transfer system, so an automatic banking craft

explanation.surface: An aeroplane that tilts into turns by itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banking' seems to be tilting in flight; it is the giro bank transfer.
explanation.definitionFit: An early rotorcraft with a freely spinning rotor, a forerunner of the helicopter.

clue.text: Magazine for ladies

definitions.meaning: a store for gunpowder on a ship or fort
a polite name for a women's toilet

explanation.surface: A periodical aimed at women readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magazine' looks like a periodical; it is an explosives store.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunpowder store and a ladies' cloakroom share this name.

clue.text: Change does include copper coin

indicators.note: include means the anagram wraps round the copper symbol
change tells us to rearrange the letters of the word does

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Someone notes that their loose change contains a copper coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like loose coins but is the anagram signal: DOES becomes ESDO, and 'include' puts CU inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The escudo was the former currency unit of Portugal, a piece of money.

clue.text: Poor sort of blood sample?

parts.note: a feeble person is called a poor example of humanity, and a phial of blood taken for testing is called the same thing

explanation.surface: A complaint about a blood sample of low quality.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sample taken for testing and, informally, a person of a given type.

clue.text: Useless material for Idle Jack

definitions.meaning: people or things that contribute nothing and can be cut away
in rummy, a jack left unmatched in a hand counts as unused, idle cards

explanation.surface: A lazy man called Jack is dismissed as good for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idle Jack' reads like a lazy person's name; it is a playing card left unused in a rummy hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Superfluous staff or items, like dried branches on a tree, and unmatched cards in rummy share this term.

clue.text: How a Slav used to proceed?

definitions.meaning: a member of a Slavic people of eastern Germany, the Sorbs
an old word meaning to go on one's way

explanation.surface: A question about how a Slavic person once made their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to' hints that the verb is an old-fashioned one, as in 'wend one's way'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sorbs of Lusatia are also called by this name, and to travel slowly is to make one's way this way.

clue.text: Bottom of the flying-class?

parts.note: Bottom is the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream, and the flying class is birds

explanation.surface: The pupil at the foot of a flying school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom' looks like last place; it is Shakespeare's Nick Bottom, a weaver by trade.
explanation.definitionFit: An African finch that builds woven nests, named for its craft.

clue.text: Colloidal stabiliser sorts out endless flu miseries

indicators.note: sorts out tells us to put the jumbled letters into a fresh order
endless means the word miseries loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone resolves a long run of miserable flu symptoms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts MISERIES to MISERIE; 'sorts out' rearranges FLU plus MISERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Such an additive keeps a mixture of oil and water from separating, as in mayonnaise.

clue.text: Revert to scenic railway

definitions.meaning: change suddenly back to an earlier state
a fairground ride of steep rises and drops

explanation.surface: Going back to a picturesque railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: A scenic railway is an old British name for a roller coaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A roller coaster and a sudden reversal of course share this name.

clue.text: In which lots of people get knocked down

definitions.text: In which lots of people get knocked down

parts.words: In which lots of people get knocked down
parts.note: sounds like a mass accident, but lots are items for sale and being knocked down means sold under the hammer

explanation.surface: A scene where many pedestrians are run over.
explanation.definitionFit: At a sale by bidding, each lot is knocked down by the gavel to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Collect after this: treble works?

parts.note: the collect is a short church prayer and a treble is a boy soprano, so a young chorister sings before the prayer

explanation.surface: Instructions to gather something once a triple effort is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collect' is a church prayer and 'treble' a high boy's voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy singing treble in a church or cathedral choir.

clue.text: Devilishly sticky game

parts.note: the toy's name comes from the Italian for devil, and it is played with two sticks and a string

explanation.surface: A game described as fiendishly tricky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticky' seems to mean awkward; it means played with sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: This juggling toy is a spool spun on a string held between two hand sticks.

clue.text: Chaff not recommended for the elderly

explanation.surface: Husks unsuitable as food for old people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chaff' looks like husks; it means teasing banter.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful teasing talk, banter.

clue.text: Beam, sort of square,---over manor's crooked

indicators.note: over sets the letter above the rest in this down entry

parts.note: a T-square is a draughtsman's ruler

indicators.note: crooked means the letters of manor's are bent out of order

explanation.surface: A beam at a manor house is not quite square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' rearranges MANORS into RANSOM, placed under T.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbar over a door or window, or across a boat's stern, is a horizontal timber.

clue.text: Get cornice moulded, oblivious to other views

indicators.note: moulded tells us the letters are shaped into a new form

explanation.surface: An instruction to have a decorative ceiling cornice moulded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moulded' looks like plasterwork; it rearranges GET plus CORNICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-centred person thinks only of their own perspective, ignoring anyone else's.

clue.text: Measure of the spirit of melodrama

indicators.note: the spirit of points to letters sitting at the heart of the word melodrama

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up how much theatrical spirit a melodrama holds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' also hints at whisky, which this small measure usually holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tot of whisky or other liquor is a standard pouring quantity.

clue.text: Put forward claim for a shelf, say

indicators.note: say signals that we go by how the words are spoken

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: Lodging a claim for a shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert something without proof is to state it as a charge.

clue.text: Capital complex castle defence

definitions.meaning: an arts and housing complex in the City of London
a fortified outer gateway guarding a castle

explanation.surface: A complicated set of defences around a capital city's castle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Barbican is a large arts centre and estate in London, Britain's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: London's arts estate took its name from the outer fortification of a medieval gatehouse.

clue.text: Evidence of worm's writhing acts

indicators.note: writhing means the letters of acts twist into a new order

explanation.surface: A worm writhes about, leaving evidence of its doings.
explanation.walkthrough: Earthworms leave coiled heaps of soil on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A worm leaves a coil of excreted earth on lawns as a sign it is there.

clue.text: Salt needed for cockles and mussels, right?

parts.note: shellfish are food from the ocean

explanation.surface: Asking whether salt should be added to a plate of cockles and mussels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' seems to be seasoning; it is an old sailor, as in 'old salt'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is a veteran sailor, a person who travels by ship.

clue.text: Such a scholar has written verse with right hand

explanation.surface: A scholar who writes poetry and is right-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhodes Scholarships send students to Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford award named after Cecil Rhodes makes its holders this kind of scholar.

clue.text: Watch the factory record-holder

definitions.meaning: a clock or wristwatch keeping the hour
the clerk who logs workers' hours at a works

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on the person who holds the factory's record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record-holder' suggests a champion; it is the person who records staff hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a chronometer and the official noting hours worked or race times carry this title.
